412	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
413	# Parsed expression tree
414	#
415	# Node tuples:
416	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
417	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
418	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
419	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
420	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
421	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
422	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
423	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
424	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
425	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
426	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
427	#   ("not", operand)
428	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
429	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
430	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
431	#
432	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
433	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
434	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
435	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
436	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
437	
438	
439	@dataclass(frozen=True)
440	class _RefItem:
441	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
442	
443	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
444	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
445	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
446	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
447	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
448	    descending: bool = False
449	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
450	    # Table qualifiers (two-table queries only; None when unqualified):
451	    table: str | None = None
452	    table_quoted: bool = False
453	    arg_table: str | None = None
454	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
455	
456	
457	@dataclass(frozen=True)
458	class _Join:
459	    """The single optional equi-join of a two-table query."""
460	
461	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left"
462	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
463	    table_quoted: bool
464	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
465	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
466	
467	
468	@dataclass
469	class _Select:
470	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
471	    table: str
472	    table_quoted: bool
473	    where: tuple | None
474	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
475	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
476	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
477	    having: tuple | None
478	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
479	    limit: int | None
480	    join: _Join | None = None
481	
482	    @property
483	    def star(self) -> bool:
484	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
485	
486	    @property
487	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
488	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
489	
490	    @property
491	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
492	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None
493

495	class _Parser:
496	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
497	
498	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
499	        self.tokens = tokens
500	        self.pos = 0
501	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
502	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
503	        # them as syntax errors.
504	        self._allow_join = allow_join
505	
506	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
507	        select = self._parse_select()
508	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
509	            tok = self._peek()
510	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
511	        return select
512	
513	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
514	        self._expect_keyword("select")
515	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
516	        self._expect_keyword("from")
517	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
518	        join = None
519	        if self._allow_join:
520	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
521	                self._expect_keyword("join")
522	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
523	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
524	                self._expect_keyword("join")
525	                join = self._parse_join("left")
526	        where = None
527	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
528	            where = self._parse_or()
529	        group_by = None
530	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
531	            self._expect_keyword("by")
532	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
533	            while self._accept_op(","):
534	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
535	            group_by = tuple(names)
536	        having = None
537	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
538	            having = self._parse_having_or()
539	        order_by = None
540	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
541	            self._expect_keyword("by")
542	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
543	            while self._accept_op(","):
544	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
545	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
546	        limit = None
547	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
548	            limit = self._parse_limit()
549	        return _Select(
550	            items=items,
551	            table=table_tok.value,
552	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
553	            where=where,
554	            group_by=group_by,
555	            having=having,
556	            order_by=order_by,
557	            limit=limit,
558	            join=join,
559	        )
560	
561	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
562	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
563	        self._expect_keyword("on")
564	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
565	        self._expect_op("=")
566	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
567	        return _Join(
568	            kind=kind,
569	            table=table_tok.value,
570	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
571	            left_key=left_key,
572	            right_key=right_key,
573	        )
574	
575	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
576	        tok = self._peek()
577	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
578	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
579	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
580	            )
581	        self._next()
582	        if not self._accept_op("."):
583	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
584	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
585	            )
586	        nxt = self._peek()
587	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
588	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
589	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
590	            )
591	        self._next()
592	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
593	
594	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
595	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
596	        while self._accept_op(","):
597	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
598	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
599	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
600	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
601	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
602	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
603	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
604	        tok = self._peek()
605	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
606	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
607	        ):
608	            grouped_ahead = any(
609	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
610	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
611	            )
612	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
613	                raise QueryValidationError(
614	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
615	                )
616	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
617	        return items
618	
619	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
620	        tok = self._peek()
621	        if tok.kind == "star":
622	            self._next()
623	            return _RefItem("star")
624	        if (
625	            tok.kind == "ident"
626	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
627	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
628	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
629	        ):
630	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
631	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
632	                raise QueryValidationError(
633	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
634	                )
635	            return item
636	        node = self._parse_arith()
637	        if node[0] == "column":
638	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
639	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
640	            return _RefItem(
641	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
642	            )
643	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
644	        self._expect_keyword("as")
645	        alias = self._peek()
646	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
647	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
648	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
649	            )
650	        self._next()
651	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
652	
653	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
654	        tok = self._peek()
655	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
656	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
657	        )
658	
659	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
660	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
661	        descending = False
662	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
663	            descending = False
664	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
665	            descending = True
666	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
667	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
668	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
669	                nulls_first = True
670	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
671	                nulls_first = False
672	            else:
673	                tok = self._peek()
674	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
675	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
676	                )
677	        return _RefItem(
678	            item.kind,
679	            name=item.name,
680	            func=item.func,
681	            arg=item.arg,
682	            descending=descending,
683	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
684	            table=item.table,
685	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
686	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
687	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
688	        )
689	
690	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
691	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
692	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
693	
694	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
695	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
696	        table_tok = self._next()
697	        self._expect_op(".")
698	        name_tok = self._peek()
699	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
700	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
701	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
702	            )
703	        self._next()
704	        return _RefItem(
705	            "column",
706	            name=name_tok.value,
707	            table=table_tok.value,
708	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
709	        )
710	
711	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
712	        tok = self._peek()
713	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
714	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
715	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
716	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
717	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
718	        # can only be a plain column reference.
719	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
720	            self._next()
721	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
722	        func = tok.value.lower()
723	        self._next()  # consume the function name
724	        if not self._accept_op("("):
725	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
726	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
727	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
728	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
729	        self._expect_op(")")
730	        return _RefItem(
731	            "agg",
732	            func=func.upper(),
733	            arg=arg,
734	            arg_table=arg_table,
735	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
736	        )
737	
738	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
739	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
740	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
741	        # name "" stands for '*'.
742	        tok = self._peek()
743	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
744	            raise QueryValidationError(
745	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
746	            )
747	        if tok.kind == "star":
748	            if func != "count":
749	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
750	            self._next()
751	            return ("", None, False)
752	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
753	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
754	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
755	            )
756	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
757	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
758	            nxt = self._peek()
759	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
760	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
761	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
762	                )
763	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
764	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
765	        self._next()
766	        nxt = self._peek()
767	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
768	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
769	                raise QueryValidationError(
770	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
771	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
772	                )
773	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
774	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
775	            )
776	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
777	        return (tok.value, None, False)
778	
779	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
780	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
781	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
782	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
783	            raise QueryValidationError(
784	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
785	            )
786	
787	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
788	        tok = self._peek()
789	        if (
790	            tok.kind != "number"
791	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
792	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
793	        ):
794	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
795	        self._next()
796	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
797	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
798	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
799	            )
800	        return tok.value
801	
802	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
803	        tok = self._peek()
804	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
805	            return self._next()
806	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
807	
808	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
809	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
810	        tok = self._peek()
811	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
812	            raise QueryValidationError(
813	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
814	            )
815	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
816	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
817	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
818	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
819	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
820	        else:
821	            self._next()
822	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
823	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
824	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
825	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
826	            raise QueryValidationError(
827	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
828	            )
829	        return result

831	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
832	    #
833	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
834	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
835	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
836	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
837	
838	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
839	        node = self._parse_having_and()
840	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
841	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
842	        return node
843	
844	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
845	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
846	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
847	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
848	        return node
849	
850	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
851	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
852	        tok = self._peek()
853	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
854	            self._next()
855	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
856	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
857	        return left
858	
859	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
860	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
861	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
862	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
863	
864	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
865	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
866	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
867	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
868	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
869	            raise QueryValidationError(
870	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
871	            )
872	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
873	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
874	            self._expect_keyword("null")
875	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
876	        return node
877	
878	    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
879	        tok = self._peek()
880	        if self._accept_op("("):
881	            node = self._parse_having_or()
882	            self._expect_op(")")
883	            return node
884	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
885	            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
886	            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
887	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
888	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
889	                self._next()
890	                self._next()
891	                value = nxt.value
892	                if isinstance(value, int):
893	                    if tok.value == "-":
894	                        value = -value
895	                    if not (_INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX):
896	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
897	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
898	                        )
899	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
900	                return ("literal", -value if tok.value == "-" else value, "float64")
901	            if nxt.kind == "eof":
902	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
903	                    f"expected a numeric literal after {tok.value!r} in HAVING"
904	                )
905	            raise QueryValidationError(
906	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
907	            )
908	        if tok.kind == "star":
909	            raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' is not allowed in HAVING")
910	        if tok.kind == "number":
911	            self._next()
912	            value = tok.value
913	            if isinstance(value, bool):
914	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
915	            return (
916	                "literal",
917	                value,
918	                "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64",
919	            )
920	        if tok.kind == "string":
921	            self._next()
922	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
923	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
924	            if (
925	                tok.kind == "ident"
926	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
927	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
928	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
929	            ):
930	                func = tok.value.lower()
931	                self._next()  # function name
932	                self._expect_op("(")
933	                arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
934	                self._expect_op(")")
935	                return ("hagg", func.upper(), arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted)
936	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
937	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
938	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
939	            if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
940	                self._next()
941	                return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
942	            # An aggregate-style name not followed by '(' is a plain column.
943	            self._next()
944	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
945	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
946	            if tok.value == "case":
947	                raise QueryValidationError("CASE expressions are not allowed in HAVING")
948	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
949	                f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in HAVING expression"
950	            )
951	        raise QuerySyntaxError(
952	            f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in HAVING expression"
953	        )
954	
955	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
956	
957	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
958	        node = self._parse_and()
959	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
960	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
961	        return node
962	
963	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
964	        node = self._parse_comparison()
965	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
966	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
967	        return node
968	
969	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
970	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
971	        tok = self._peek()
972	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
973	            self._next()
974	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
975	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
976	        return left
977	
978	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
979	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
980	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
981	        return self._parse_postfix()
982	
983	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
984	        node = self._parse_arith()
985	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
986	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
987	            self._expect_keyword("null")
988	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
989	        return node
990	
991	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
992	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
993	
994	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
995	        node = self._parse_term()
996	        while True:
997	            tok = self._peek()
998	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
999	                self._next()
1000	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
1001	            else:
1002	                return node
1003	
1004	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
1005	        node = self._parse_factor()
1006	        while True:
1007	            tok = self._peek()
1008	            if tok.kind == "star":
1009	                self._next()
1010	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
1011	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
1012	                self._next()

1017	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
1018	        tok = self._peek()

1020	            negate = tok.value == "-"
1021	            self._next()
1022	            nxt = self._peek()
1023	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):

1025	                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
1026	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
1027	                self._next()
1028	                value = nxt.value
1029	                if isinstance(value, int):
1030	                    if negate:
1031	                        value = -value
1032	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
1033	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
1034	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
1035	                        )
1036	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
1037	                if negate:
1038	                    value = -value
1039	                return ("literal", value, "float64")
1040	            if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident") and not (
1041	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
1042	            ) and not (nxt.kind == "keyword" and nxt.value == "case"):

1044	                    "sign must be followed by a numeric literal or expression"
1045	                )

1048	        if (

1050	            and isinstance(node[1], int)
1051	            and not isinstance(node[1], bool)

1059	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:

1070	            if isinstance(value, bool):
1071	                return ("literal", value, "bool")

1078	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():

1080	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
1081	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
1082	            if (
1083	                tok.kind == "ident"
1084	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
1085	                and nxt.kind == "op"
1086	                and nxt.value == "("
1087	            ):

1090	                )

1093	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
1094	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")

1097	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1098	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
1099	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1100	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
1101	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
1102	        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
1103	        branches: list[tuple] = []
1104	        while True:
1105	            self._expect_keyword("when")
1106	            condition = self._parse_or()
1107	            self._expect_keyword("then")
1108	            result = self._parse_arith()
1109	            branches.append((condition, result))
1110	            tok = self._peek()
1111	            if not (tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "when"):
1112	                break
1113	        else_node = None
1114	        if self._accept_keyword("else"):
1115	            else_node = self._parse_arith()
1116	        self._expect_keyword("end")

1124	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
1125	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1126	        self.pos += 1

1129	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
1130	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
1131	            self.pos += 1

1133	        return False

1135	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
1136	        tok = self._peek()
1137	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
1138	            self.pos += 1
1139	            return True
1140	        return False

1142	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1143	        tok = self._peek()
1144	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
1145	            self.pos += 1
1146	            return True
1147	        return False

1150	        tok = self._peek()

1152	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")

1155	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1156	        tok = self._peek()
1157	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
1158	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")

1331	def _bind_aggregate(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1332	    if select.star:
1333	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")
1334	
1335	    if (
1336	        select.having is not None
1337	        and select.group_by is None
1338	        and not select.has_aggregate
1339	        and not _having_tree_has_aggregate(select.having)
1340	    ):
1341	        # HAVING filters formed groups; without aggregation or GROUP BY the
1342	        # statement stays a non-aggregate query and HAVING has no meaning.
1343	        raise QueryValidationError(
1344	            "HAVING is only valid with GROUP BY or an aggregate"
1345	        )

1347	    # Resolve GROUP BY columns first: order matters for the grouping key, and
1348	    # duplicates / unknown columns are rejected here.  Entries are
1349	    # (table, table_quoted, name) triples; names reaching the binder are
1350	    # already canonical (single-file queries never carry a qualifier).
1351	    group_indices: list[int] = []

1354	        if name in group_seen:
1355	            raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate column in GROUP BY: {name!r}")

1357	        try:
1358	            group_indices.append(schema.index(name))
1359	        except KeyError:
1360	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown GROUP BY column: {name!r}") from None
1361	    group_index_set = set(group_indices)

1363	    # One registry of distinct aggregates shared by SELECT, HAVING and ORDER
1364	    # BY, keyed by (function, argument index) and kept in first-reference
1365	    # order.  HAVING-only aggregates are computed but never projected.
1366	    agg_registry: dict[tuple, int] = {}
1367	    agg_order: list[_BoundItem] = []
1368

1370	        arg_index, arg_col, label, out_type, nullable = _resolve_agg_call(
1371	            func, arg_name, schema
1372	        )
1373	        key = (func, arg_index)
1374	        slot = agg_registry.get(key)
1375	        if slot is None:
1376	            slot = len(agg_order)
1377	            agg_registry[key] = slot
1378	            agg_order.append(
1379	                _BoundItem(
1380	                    "agg",
1381	                    output_name=label,
1382	                    func=func,
1383	                    arg_index=arg_index,
1384	                    arg_type=arg_col.type if arg_col is not None else "",
1385	                    out_type=out_type,
1386	                    nullable=nullable,
1387	                )
1388	            )

1391	    # Resolve the projection.  Plain columns must be grouped; output names
1392	    # (group column names and canonical "FUNC(arg)" labels) must be unique.
1393	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
1394	    output_seen: set[str] = set()
1395	    has_plain = False
1396	    for item in select.items:
1397	        if item.kind == "star":
1398	            raise QueryValidationError(
1399	                "'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY"
1400	            )
1401	        if item.kind == "expr":
1402	            raise QueryValidationError(
1403	                "scalar expressions are not supported in aggregate queries"
1404	            )
1405	        if item.kind == "column":
1406	            has_plain = True
1407	            name = item.name
1408	            try:
1409	                col_index = schema.index(name)
1410	            except KeyError:
1411	                raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1412	            if col_index not in group_index_set:
1413	                raise QueryValidationError(
1414	                    f"column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
1415	                )
1416	            label = name
1417	            if label in output_seen:
1418	                raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate result column: {name!r}")
1419	            output_seen.add(label)
1420	            col = schema.columns[col_index]
1421	            bound_items.append(
1422	                _BoundItem(
1423	                    "column",
1424	                    output_name=label,
1425	                    col_index=col_index,
1426	                    out_type=col.type,
1427	                    nullable=col.nullable,
1428	                )

1430	        else:

1464	        "having": having,
1465	        "order_by": order_by,
1466	    }

1470	    """Whether a parsed (unbound) HAVING tree names at least one aggregate."""
1471	    tag = node[0]
1472	    if tag == "hagg":
1473	        return True
1474	    if tag in ("literal", "column"):
1475	        return False
1476	    if tag in ("not", "isnull"):
1477	        return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[1])
1478	    if tag == "cmp":
1479	        return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[2]) or _having_tree_has_aggregate(
1480	            node[3]
1481	        )
1482	    return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[1]) or _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[2])

1485	def _bind_having(
1486	    node: tuple,
1487	    schema: Schema,
1488	    group_index_set: set[int],
1489	    agg_order: list[_BoundItem],
1490	    require_aggregate,
1491	) -> tuple:
1492	    tag = node[0]
1493	    if tag == "literal":
1494	        return node
1495	    if tag == "column":
1496	        name = node[1]
1497	        try:
1498	            col_index = schema.index(name)
1499	        except KeyError:
1500	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1501	        if col_index not in group_index_set:
1502	            raise QueryValidationError(
1503	                f"HAVING column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
1504	            )
1505	        col = schema.columns[col_index]
1506	        return ("column", name, col_index, col.type, col.nullable)
1507	    if tag == "hagg":
1508	        slot = require_aggregate(node[1], node[2])
1509	        agg_item = agg_order[slot]
1510	        return ("hagg", slot, agg_item.out_type, agg_item.nullable)
1511	    if tag == "not":
1512	        operand = _bind_having(
1513	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1514	        )
1515	        _require_having_boolean(operand, "NOT")
1516	        return ("not", operand)
1517	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1518	        left = _bind_having(
1519	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1520	        )
1521	        right = _bind_having(
1522	            node[2], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1523	        )
1524	        _require_having_boolean(left, tag.upper())
1525	        _require_having_boolean(right, tag.upper())
1526	        return (tag, left, right)
1527	    if tag == "isnull":
1528	        operand = _bind_having(
1529	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1530	        )
1531	        if operand[0] not in ("literal", "column", "hagg"):
1532	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1533	                "IS NULL operand must be a group column, an aggregate or a literal"
1534	            )
1535	        return ("isnull", operand, node[2])
1536	    if tag == "cmp":
1537	        op = node[1]
1538	        left = _bind_having(
1539	            node[2], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1540	        )
1541	        right = _bind_having(
1542	            node[3], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1543	        )
1544	        if left[0] not in ("literal", "column", "hagg") or right[0] not in (
1545	            "literal",
1546	            "column",
1547	            "hagg",
1548	        ):
1549	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1550	                "comparison operands must be group columns, aggregates or literals"
1551	            )

1553	        right_t = _having_value_type(right)
1554	        if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
1555	            if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
1556	                raise QueryValidationError(
1557	                    f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1558	                )
1559	            if op not in ("=", "!="):
1560	                raise QueryValidationError(f"bool only supports = and !=, not {op!r}")

1563	                raise QueryValidationError(
1564	                    f"utf8 can only be compared to utf8, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1565	                )
